databricks-dbcu-steady.title: Compare an Azure Databricks prepurchase plan
databricks-dbcu-steady.body: These Databricks DBUs are priced pay-as-you-go and are expected to run steadily for a year or longer. Compare a one-year or three-year Databricks commit unit (DBCU) prepurchase plan sized to the monthly DBU spend; the pool is drawn down at the DBU list price. The virtual machines under classic clusters are not covered by it.

citation.source: Optimize Azure Databricks costs with a prepurchase
citation.quote: You can save on your Azure Databricks unit (DBU) costs when you prepurchase Azure Databricks commit units (DBCU) for one or three years.

databricks-job-clusters.title: Use job clusters for scheduled Databricks work
databricks-job-clusters.body: This all-purpose compute runs only part of the month, which suggests scheduled or batch work. Job clusters (Jobs compute) have a lower DBU rate and stop when the job ends.

citation.source: Architecture strategies / service guide: Azure Databricks
citation.quote: Deploy job clusters for scheduled workloads instead of all-purpose clusters to eliminate idle compute costs.

databricks-auto-termination.title: Turn on auto-termination for interactive Databricks clusters
databricks-auto-termination.body: This all-purpose compute is priced as running around the clock. Interactive clusters should auto-terminate after an idle period, so DBUs and the virtual machines under them stop billing.

citation.source: Architecture strategies / service guide: Azure Databricks
citation.quote: Set up automatic termination for all interactive clusters with appropriate timeout periods based on usage patterns.

databricks-sql-autostop.title: Turn on autostop for Databricks SQL warehouses
databricks-sql-autostop.body: This SQL warehouse is priced as running around the clock. Autostop shuts it down when idle so DBUs stop billing.

citation.source: Architecture strategies / service guide: Azure Databricks
citation.quote: turn on autostop functionality to minimize costs during inactive periods
